topic: The exact trap that stalls most developer-led startups

post.topic: The exact trap that stalls most developer-led startups
post.linkedin_text:
Building a startup isn't about writing clever code. It is about falling in love with the problem.

Too many developers start by picking a fancy tech stack for their new project.

They spend weeks setting up microservices, Docker, and Kubernetes for an app with zero users.

I have caught myself doing this too.

The fix is boring but effective:

• Write down the actual pain point in one sentence
• Build the simplest possible interface that solves it
• Ignore scalability until people are actually complaining it is slow

At JAEXS Solutions, our core rule is simple: find everyday friction, build a generic and reusable fix, and ship it before you feel ready.

What is one tech stack decision you regret making too early in a project?
